description:
op-fdph's keep-warm daemon (crates/kovan/src/commands/lsp_daemon.rs) is Unix-domain-socket-based and gated #[cfg(unix)]. On Windows, query()/serve()/stop() all resolve to the #[cfg(not(unix))] stub: query() returns None unconditionally (every caller then falls back to super::semq::connect's spawn-per-call RustAnalyzerSession path), serve() returns an error string (unreachable in practice since query() never spawns lsp-daemon-serve there), stop() just prints 'no lsp-daemon on this platform'.

This has only been reasoned about and compiled for (this dev machine is Linux; no Windows CI in this workspace per CLAUDE.md), never actually run on Windows. Needs verification on a real Windows machine (or at minimum a Windows CI runner if one gets added) that:
1. kovan-cli def/sig/refs actually work end-to-end via the spawn-per-call fallback (RustAnalyzerSession::connect_with_observed spawning rust-analyzer.exe, hover/references round-tripping correctly) -- nothing here is Windows-specific in that path's own code, but it has never been exercised on that OS.
2. kovan-cli lsp-daemon-stop's stub prints its message and exits 0 cleanly rather than erroring.
3. cargo build/test for the kovan crate (all three binaries) succeeds on a Windows target at all, given the new kopitiam-semantic/kopitiam-tokenizer dependencies (both already confirmed lightweight/pure-Rust by their own Cargo.toml deps, but not yet cross-checked against a live Windows toolchain).

Not blocking -- the design already treats 'no daemon on Windows' as an explicit, intentional fallback rather than a silent gap (see the module's own 'Platform scope' doc section) -- but the fallback path itself needs a real run to confirm, not just an argument that it should work.
title: kovan-cli: verify lsp-daemon's Windows fallback path on a real Windows machine
